My goal is scalar easly maintenacne, robustness and powerfull code for create a very comprehensive calendar table with all the date Below is a theoretical, structured recommendation of additional columns you should consider adding to your calendar table, based strictly on best practices observed in enterprise data warehouses, BI systems, financial modeling, and scheduling analytics.

Your existing list is already rich, so the suggestions focus on high-value fields that are commonly expected but not yet explicitly listed in your description.

✅ High-Value Calendar Columns You Should Add
1. Interoperability & Master Key Columns

These help when joining with external systems or dimension tables.

Surrogate Date Keys

date_key (int, YYYYMMDD)

datetime_key (int, YYYYMMDDHHMMSS)

Why:
Used in data warehouses (star schemas), ensures fast joins and avoids datetime comparison issues.

2. ISO-Standard Columns (Widely Used)

You have week information, but ISO standards are often mandatory for analytics.

iso_year

iso_week

iso_day (1–7)

Why:
Many BI tools and corporate reports use ISO 8601 weeks instead of standard week numbering.

3. Month/Quarter Boundary Flags (Crucial for Reporting Automation)

You have some boundary flags, but these extend completeness.

is_first_day_of_month

is_last_day_of_quarter

is_first_day_of_quarter

is_first_day_of_year

is_last_day_of_fiscal_period

is_first_day_of_fiscal_period

Why:
Used in ETL workflows, month-end reporting, accruals, and automated rollovers.

4. Rolling Window Features (Machine Learning Friendly)

These columns help forecasting models and time-based features.

day_of_year (1–365/366)

week_of_year (non-ISO)

rolling_7_day_group

rolling_30_day_group

rolling_365_day_group

Why:
Essential for time-series feature engineering.

5. Workload & Workforce Scheduling Columns

Strongly used in HR analytics, hospital planning, and production systems.

is_workday_flex (company-specific rule)

shift_period (morning/afternoon/night)

is_payroll_cutoff_day

biweekly_period_number (1–26 per year)

Why:
Prevents custom logic repeated in downstream applications.

6. Multi-Calendar Alignment Columns

Useful when combining multiple calendars (retail, fiscal, academic).

academic_year_start

academic_year (e.g., 2024-2025)

academic_semester

retail_year (52–53 week models)

Why:
Academic and retail calendars differ from standard calendars and are widely needed in global orgs.

7. Timezone-Sensitive Columns (If Not Already Included)

You already have some regional columns, but these add full coverage:

utc_offset_minutes

is_ambiguous_time (DST transition ambiguities)

is_imaginary_time (DST skip hours)

Why:
Prevents timestamp errors during DST handling and log ingestion.

8. Seasonality Columns (Widely Used in Forecasting + Reporting)

season (winter/spring/summer/fall, hemisphere-based)

meteorological_season

heating_season_flag

cooling_season_flag

Why:
Essential for energy, climate, supply chain, and sales forecasting.

9. International Business & Finance Columns

These are extremely useful if you support multi-country operations.

is_end_of_financial_quarter (country-specific)

is_settlement_day (banks)

is_fx_market_holiday

is_stock_market_holiday (by region)

Why:
Supports finance departments and trading systems.

10. Holidays with Categories

You have holiday flags, but modern systems use tagged holidays.

holiday_name

holiday_category (public holiday, religious, national, bank holiday)

holiday_type (fixed, floating, lunar calendar, Islamic, etc.)

Why:
Allows downstream systems to handle holidays without hardcoded logic.

⭐ Top 10 Highest-Impact Columns to Add (If You Want a Short List)

date_key (YYYYMMDD)

iso_year / iso_week / iso_day

day_of_year

is_first_day_of_month / is_last_day_of_month

is_first_day_of_quarter / is_last_day_of_quarter

holiday_name / holiday_category

season / meteorological_season

utc_offset_minutes / is_ambiguous_time

biweekly_period_number

is_settlement_day / is_stock_market_holiday

These offer broad value across data engineering, reporting, forecasting, finance, and operations.
